question: What is the prevalence of hypereosinophilia?
refined_question: Among noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years), what is the survey-weighted prevalence of hypereosinophilia (absolute eosinophil count >=1.5 x10^9/L (ICOG-EO / WHO threshold)), overall and by sex and age group?
title: Prevalence of Hypereosinophilia Among US Adults: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic
hypothesis: Hypereosinophilia is common in this population and varies by sex and age group.

pico.population: noninstitutionalized US participants in NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic (Age >=18 years)
pico.exposure: Not applicable (descriptive prevalence); subgroups: Sex and Age group
pico.covariates: Sex, Age group, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, and Body mass index

model.rationale: Prevalence estimand: survey-weighted proportions with Korn-Graubard (beta) 95% CIs, overall and by subgroup, assessed against NCHS presentation standards; population counts from weighted totals. Adjusted correlates are estimated with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression (prevalence ratios).

missing_data.rationale: Complete-case primary analysis within the design; multiple imputation by chained equations as sensitivity analysis when covariates are missing.

rationale.statistician: Prevalence estimand: survey-weighted proportions with Korn-Graubard (beta) 95% CIs, overall and by subgroup, assessed against NCHS presentation standards; population counts from weighted totals. Adjusted correlates are estimated with survey-weighted quasi-Poisson regression (prevalence ratios).
rationale.epidemiologist: Correlates model includes Age, Sex, Race and ethnicity, Income-to-poverty ratio, and Body mass index to describe independent associations with hypereosinophilia - absolute eosinophil count >=1.5 x10^9/L; these are descriptive, not causal, contrasts. Variables on the causal pathway or sharing laboratory components with the outcome/exposure are excluded to avoid over-adjustment.

limitations: Cross-sectional design: temporality cannot be established and associations must not be interpreted causally.
Single measurement of laboratory values; within-person variability and chronicity cannot be assessed.
Residual confounding by unmeasured or imperfectly measured factors (e.g., diet, medications, menstrual blood loss).
Self-reported comorbidities and behaviours are subject to recall and social-desirability bias.
NHANES excludes institutionalized and active-duty military populations.

Operational definition (AEC >=1.5): ICOG-EO requires >1.5 x10^9/L on two examinations at least 1 month apart (or tissue hypereosinophilia); NHANES has one CBC, so this is single-measurement hypereosinophilia.
Operational definition (AEC >=1.5): Very rare in the general population - expect wide confidence intervals and possible NCHS suppression; consider eosinophilia (>=0.5) as the primary outcome.
